113	## Detailed Design
114	
115	### Core Rules
116	
117	Rule ids are `DA-n`. Lint ids are SCREAMING_SNAKE without a prefix (Layout's convention); `FIXTURE_COUNT_ROOM` and `FIXTURE_COUNT_WORLD` are used verbatim because Layout assigned them to this system. Formula ids `D.n` are this GDD's (Layout's are written `LY D.n`, the Graph's `LSG D.n`, and so on). Locked constants are used by registry name with their registry value; a number resting on a provisional upstream carries `[PLACEHOLDER: owner]` at every mention. Lines marked *(orchestrator ruling: ...)* record where the specialists disagreed and which reading this GDD adopts. **Formula index** (fixed here so the Formulas section does not renumber): D.1 tile volume budget per reachable set; D.2 count tolerance (one-sided); D.3 fixture bound use; D.4 part cover use and access order; D.5 escape-route use (run, walk, carry); D.6 residual-light clock, recharge and withdrawal; D.7 traverse bound use; D.8 containment colour count; D.9 PWR-OVL window, trigger and trunk cap; D.10 cold-room exposure budget; D.11 dead-fault back-date; D.12 fault-glow cascade bound; D.13 weld offset; D.14 leaky-kind wear clock; D.15 patch and fatigue treadmills; D.16 derelict A bus-on-battery window; D.17 reachable-set subject budget; D.18 thermal drift (the cold-room invariant); D.19 cryo-bay and ship air clocks; D.20 B's fatigue clock; D.21 B's restart reservoir floor; D.22 heater on the bus battery (A's warm window) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*.
118	
119	#### A. Scope, roster, files, wear
120	
121	**DA-1 Authoring is content, not runtime.** Derelict Authoring registers no state block (kernel CR-8), no step hook (CR-3), no mutator and no read_view. It owns the authored files, the kit manifest, the CONTENT lint and the ledgers. Its runtime consumers are Layout (`build_section`), the Graph (M1 `instantiate_section`), the Emitter (E1 `instantiate_section_emitters`) and Interaction (`place_loose`, `sync_section`), named in Interactions with Other Systems. Consequences: there is nothing to snapshot, no `schema_version` of its own and no kernel amendment; systems stay scene-tree free (kernel H10), so every lint and every content acceptance run is headless.
122	
123	**DA-2 Roster: three ship templates, one role each.** (registry: `mvp_template_roster`) All three are `dialect: foundry`, `rot_q` 0 (no rotation, no mirror), `SECTION_SCHEMA_VERSION` 1. **Ring hint:** Authoring authors no ring hint in MVP; all four templates resolve to ring 1 by AT-6 (3) unless Web Map & Transit publishes a ring. A `ring_hint` field, if later wanted, is a Layout schema ask (new OQ-DA-29), never a content field minted here.
124	
125	| `template_id` | Role | Kind | Rooms | Sockets | `entry_room_key` (the room the pod arrives in) | Sortie order (a recommendation, never a gate) |
126	|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
127	| `home_ship` | the derelict the player wakes in (cryo bay); the base that grows | HOME | 5 | 1 (`sock_airlock_e`) | `airlock` | start |
128	| `derelict_a` | cold wreck; salvage only; never welded | DERELICT | 4 | 0 | `a_dock` | first sortie |
129	| `derelict_b` | hot wreck; the weld donor | DERELICT | 5 | 1 (`sock_b_w`) | `b_dock` | second sortie |
130	
131	The index's "two handmade derelicts" are `derelict_a` and `derelict_b`; the spawn ship is `home_ship`. Derelict A yields a **module** (the failed scrubber at `hp` 2000, the first V8, with the spare breaker and the heater beside it), never a section; derelict B yields the **welded section** at `sock_b_w`. Derelict A is never welded, so it is only ever loaded beside a home body, never merged. Every built section starts on its own body and every multi-section body is produced by welds only (LY-25). The sortie order is an authored recommendation (A's salvage makes B's weld survivable, DA-25); freedom of sortie order is an anti-pillar-level promise (no scripted gate), and DA-32 therefore lints the post-weld sortie to A as a reachable loaded set. (orchestrator ruling: R1/R2 decide the roster and the donor; Layout LY-13 names B as the mate of the home-ship's socket three times against one clause in a Graph acceptance criterion; routed wording fixes are listed under CONFLICT headings in Cross-References.)
132	
133	**DA-3 The pod stub and the spawn table (Ship Body & Interior Physics designed; provisional — Web Map & Transit undesigned).** Ship Body (BDY-25) rules that the pod hop is a body transfer and that **the pod is a Layout body built from a pod template**, and (BDY-20, Interactions row) that Authoring owns the spawn table converted by `init_world`. This GDD therefore authors a fourth, minimal template `pod` (one room `pod_cabin`, 2 x 2 tiles, `V` 4, no fixture, no module node, one seat cell, no loose slot; its Layout `kind`, whether it is exempt from `fixtures_min` 1 and whether `room_at` answers NONE on it are Layout's and Web Map & Transit's calls, OQ-DA-17). It adds 4 tiles to `D.1` once the persistent pod body exists (built at `init_world`, never per hop, section always dormant; registry `pod_body`) and counts one body against `MAX_BODIES` 8. The spawn table is data:
134	
135	| `spawn_id` | Template, room | Section-local px (design target) | Consumed by | Rule |
136	|---|---|---|---|---|
137	| `spawn_cryo_1` | `home_ship`, `cryo_bay` | (216, 168) | `init_world` wake, seat 1 | the player's open pod row; the cell is clear of `door_cryo_s`'s approach square and of the coolant floor run |
138	| `arrive_home_airlock` | `home_ship`, `airlock` | (552, 696) | Transit pod arrival | one tile clear east of the docked-podcraft prop |
139	| `arrive_a_dock` | `derelict_a`, `a_dock` | (168, 336) | Transit pod arrival | one tile clear of the docked-podcraft prop at the room's west wall |
140	| `arrive_b_dock` | `derelict_b`, `b_dock` | (168, 312) | Transit pod arrival | as above; after the weld this room is also the seam room |
141	| `seat_pod_1` | `pod`, `pod_cabin` | (72, 48) | Transit | Ship Body's illustrative cell |
142	
143	Co-op seats 2 to 4 are Vertical Slice and are not authored (PlayerIds start at 1, KRN; seat 0 is Body's "no seat", BDY-7). Lint `SPAWN_BLOCKED` (ERROR, CI): each spawn passes Body's `can_place` (`BDY_PLACE_INSIDE_FOOTPRINT`) against Layout's rect set, the room is breathable at step 0, and no spawn lies within 1 tile of a fault's maximum floor run. Per the user ruling on D60 (2026-10-27, Web Map & Transit: crew statuses keep running while seated in the pod, and a death in the pod is the Controller's DEAD), the stub authors no atmosphere, no Graph node, no hazard and no fixture, so nothing in the pod can hurt the crew from the content side; any status consequence while seated is Suit's and the Controller's, never an authored fact *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*
144	
145	**DA-4 Files, ids and the world file.** Templates are `assets/data/sections/home_ship.json`, `derelict_a.json`, `derelict_b.json`, `pod.json`; the world file is `assets/data/world/mvp_world.json` (LY-25), listing `{template_id, kind, world_slot}` for each. `template_id` and `room_key` values are the stable strings in the tables below; renaming one after the first external build needs a migration step in the owner (LY-6 e, SL-14), and pre-release saves are disposable. Authoring adds to Layout's records only these CONTENT fields (nothing else; every other field is Layout's LY-4 and is cited by record kind, never restated): `def_id`, `hp`, `fail_since_step`, `forced_mode`, `switch_on`, `residual`, `count`, `condition_bp`, `visible_unknown`, `socket_tag`, plus the initial values of the Graph's own persisted fields listed in the mapping table below. Those last are **not new schema** (guard rail G1): each is the authored initial value of one field the Graph already persists (LS-3, LS-21), named here by its owner field.
146	
147	| Authored initial value (this GDD's shorthand) | Owner field it initialises | Unit and form | Used in |
148	|---|---|---|---|
149	| `charge` | BATTERY `stock` | integer dJ (never a percent; `BATT_CELL` 3,600,000 dJ is only the derivation base) | DA-19, DA-27, DA-35 |
150	| `valve_open` | VALVE edge `open` | bool | DA-35 |
151	| `stock` (air) | O2_TANK `stock` | integer mGU | DA-35 |
152	| `stock` (coolant, fuel) | RESERVOIR `stock_ml`, FUEL_TANK `stock_ml` | integer mL | DA-35 |
153	| `T0` | COMPARTMENT `T` | integer mC | C.1 to C.3 |
154	| `breaker_closed` | CABLE_JUNCTION `breaker_closed` | bool (already the Graph's name, LS-3) | DA-35 |
155	| `hp`, `forced_mode`, `fail_since_step` | node `hp`, `forced_mode`, `fail_since_step` | bp; enum; signed steps (OQ-DA-1) | DA-17, DA-19 |
156	| `switch_on` | Emitter FIXTURE `switch_on` (Emitter E1 placement field) | bool | DA-22 |
157	| `count` | ItemInstance `count` (Item DB; 1 for modules, parts and curios, the stack for glowsticks) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix: Item DB IDB-15, IA-28, G1/G6)* | integer | DA-26 |
158	| `condition_bp` | the loose item's ItemInstance `condition_bp` (Item DB; 1..10000 for a module, 0 for every other def; expanded by `fresh_instance`, then placed through Interaction's `place_loose`) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix: Item DB IDB-15, IA-28, G1/G6)* | integer bp | DA-26 |
159	
160	The shorthand words `charge`, `valve_open`, `stock` and `T0` are used in the room and state tables below; the table above is the one-to-one map, so no file carries a field the owners do not already define. Every authored number is an integer; `AUTHORED_NON_INTEGER` (ERROR) rejects a float, because the engine's JSON parser returns numbers as floats and the loader casts and bound-checks `[UNV: float behaviour in 4.7.2, spike]`.
161	
162	**DA-5 Dialect and wear: the `_worn` kit.** All three ships use Foundry pieces. `home_ship` uses the maintained atlas; both wrecks use the `_worn` atlas (art bible 8.5 naming `<cat>[_<dialect>]_<subject>[_<variant tokens>]_<map>.png`). The PROJECTOR picks an atlas by `template_id`, so the slice names and `layout.json` are shared and **no Layout field carries wear** (LY:1099); a decal-overlay approach was rejected because it would need a record kind Layout lacks. `_worn` is a closed vocabulary (registry: `worn_variant_token`): **scuff-to-bare at rounded corners, dust (matte Graphite mid, never a third floor value), crevice darkening (Void Steel, one value step) and clogged grates**. It excludes scorch, soot, char, rust, warm stains and any stain of a loop's fluid, because those are Graph trails and a static decal of one is a loop-vocabulary decal that is not a Graph fault (FT-3, FT AC-44) and, for soot, a false hot-room history (P1). (orchestrator ruling: R23 listed "scorch/soot" in the wear vocabulary and the level-designer's draft repeated it; the art-director's V-1 narrowing is adopted, because the same draft's DA-32 and FT AC-44 forbid exactly that decal.) Hue-less tool scorch on a cut leaf or a cut hull piece is the crew's cutter, a kit state exempt from this rule (VA-8, DA-39). Kit wear (this rule, template-driven, never changes at runtime) and module condition (authored `hp`, changes at runtime) are two axes and must never be mixed: a worn wall around a pristine module and a dark failed module in a maintained room are both legal. This answers Layout OQ-25 at MVP; the art-director's acceptance gate is AC-V3 (Acceptance Criteria) and, if the art spike cannot meet it, X-1 is downgraded to Vertical Slice as LY:1099 allows rather than left unsupported. Lint `WEAR_TOKEN_MISMATCH` (ERROR, CI): a wreck template referencing a maintained piece, or `home_ship` referencing a `_worn` piece.
163	
164	**DA-6 One meaning of `entry_room_key`.** It names the room the pod arrives in: `airlock`, `a_dock`, `b_dock`. The arrival is a presentation transition owned by Web Map & Transit (provisional); no pod hatch is a socket. Each of these rooms carries a docked-podcraft placeholder prop (kit gap K-3, DA-38). This GDD never calls derelict A "spawn". Each of the three props also carries the dock status glow of DA-46 (user ruling X2) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*. The airlock carries two console anchors (POD, DOCK); `a_dock` and `b_dock` carry one POD anchor each (OQ-DA-39, DA-46) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*.
165	
166	#### B. Geometry: rooms, doors, sockets, hull, hardpoints
167	
168	**DA-7 Room sizing by role.** Rooms are sized to the art bible's density table and to Layout's bounds, not to the Lighting C3 placeholder (DA-31). Every room: `V` within 4 to 200 tiles, each section within `SECTION_MAX_TILES_W` 48 x `SECTION_MAX_TILES_H` 32 and at most `MAX_ROOMS_PER_SECTION` 8 rooms (the worst section here has 5). Corridors are 3 tiles across (144 px, the `CORRIDOR_HEAD_NARROW` head clearance, so no corridor anchor can fail that rule). Machine rooms are at most 5 tiles deep (PIPE:874). A room deeper than `ROOM_DEPTH_SOFT_MAX` 5 or wider than `ROOM_WIDTH_SOFT_MAX` 12 carries `frame_exception` true (Layout's `ROOM_EXCEEDS_FRAME` is a WARN silenced by it): `cryo_bay` (depth 6), `spine_corridor` (13 wide), `cargo_bay` (depth 6), `a_spine` (11 deep) and `b_spine` (13 deep), five exceptions logged in the room tables. Every wall-flush kit piece has face height at most 72 px (PIPE:1068; `SOUTH_BAND_OCCUPIED` is Layout's WARN, cited). `exposed_tiles` values in the room tables are **design targets** computed by the convention of Layout's cryo fixture (one count per hull side, so a corner tile counts on both sides); the converter's D.4 value governs across 24 px lattice jogs (`EXPOSED_DRIFT` WARN, OQ-DA-13).
169	
170	**DA-8 Door grammar: every door fits LY D.18 by construction.** A door assembly (frame plus hinge-side pocket) is 192 px on a straight wall run plus `DOOR_CORNER_MARGIN_PX` 48 on the non-hinge side, so a wall carrying a door offers a straight run of at least 240 px (5 tiles). Authored consequences: (a) no door on the 3-tile end of a corridor, doors sit on corridor long sides; (b) every room hosting a door shares at least 5 tiles of straight wall with its neighbour; (c) every hatch room has a 5-tile straight hull run; (d) with hinge LOW (interior doors and socket hatches alike; `HATCH_HINGE_AUTHORED` is an error), the door assembly occupies [`doorway_start_px` - 96, `doorway_start_px` + 96) and leaves at least `DOOR_CORNER_MARGIN_PX` 48 of straight run beyond its non-hinge end (LY D.18). Every door has `width_px` 96 and `area_max` 64 (the default; range 32 to 128). Door initial state is CLOSED except where a room table says OPEN. Door leaf art states used in MVP are **closed and open only**: the cut and welded leaf states stay in the kit for the socket seam and the Vertical Slice, because welded is a socket-seam state (LY-15) and cut is a verb result with no MVP Interaction verb for an interior door. **User ruling X1 (2026-10-27): weld, the player's seam cut and install are all MVP, so the socket seam's WELDED and CUT_OPEN states, and their leaf pieces, are live MVP states at the two sockets; interior doors still carry closed and open only, and OQ-DA-10 (a lock verb for interior doors) stands** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*. A leaf that looks welded yet opens is the world lying. (orchestrator ruling: R18/R23 (iv) allowed "closed/open/cut/welded" interior states and "welded shut from inside" as a verdict; the level-designer's narrowing is adopted, supported by the creative-director and art-director, and the "welded shut from inside" kit gap (iv) has no MVP piece.)
171	
172	**DA-9 Topology is a tree; a return path always exists.** Each template's room adjacency through doors is a tree (cycle count 0; `ROOM_GRAPH_CYCLE` WARN), because one authored retreat per room is legible (P2) and the Graph rejects power-wiring cycles in MVP (LSG OQ 11). From every room there is a door path to `entry_room_key` treating doors as traversable (Layout's `ROOM_UNREACHABLE` covers reachability; `RETURN_PATH_TRAVERSE` covers the vacuum- or cold-bounded return, DA-28).
173	
174	**DA-10 Sockets, lanes and the weld offset.** Exactly one socket on `home_ship`, one on `derelict_b`, none on `derelict_a`; `MAX_SOCKETS_PER_SECTION` is 4 and `SOCKET_SPACING_MIN_TILES` 2 is moot. Both sockets carry `class_id` 1 (`SOCKET_CLASS`, `DOCK_STD`), `socket_tag` `dock_std` (an authoring convenience; port types are authoritative, IDB:169), `width_tiles` 2, **lane 0 `{POWER, lane_index 0}`, lane 1 `{O2, lane_index 0}`** and one hatch (Modular Ship Assembly, on disk and In Design, repeats the lane set and the offset in MSA-11; `socket_plan` and `apply` are Layout's and `can_join` is the Graph's). There is **no COOLANT lane** in MVP: it would join the home reactor's coolant loop to B's leaking loop at the first weld, a hazard beyond "one weld" and beyond the eight faults. Layout's `fixture_airlock` and `fixture_derelict_b_socket` carry COOLANT + POWER lanes as "fixture content, not a design decision" (LY:1258); they are schema examples and are **not changed** (stated in Cross-References so no one files a conflict). The Graph's `can_join` rejects `PORT_INCOMPAT` (LS-15), so each lane's node must be real and expose the matching port type; the lane nodes sit in the dock rooms so the seam edge stays far under `TRAIL_EDGE_MAX_PX` 1152.
175	
176	| Socket | Section | Facing | `line_px` | `start_px` (span) | Hatch | POWER lane node | O2 lane node |
177	|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
178	| `sock_airlock_e` | `home_ship`, `airlock` | E | 720 | 672 (y 672 to 768) | `door_airlock_e` | `j_main` (CABLE_JUNCTION) | `dj_air` (DUCT_JUNCTION, bare) |
179	| `sock_b_w` | `derelict_b`, `b_dock` | W | 24 | 288 (y 288 to 384) | `door_b_hatch_w` | `j_b_main` (CABLE_JUNCTION) | `dj_b_dock` (DUCT_JUNCTION, bare) |
180	
181	The mating predicate order is Layout's (`SOCKET_UNKNOWN`, `SOCKET_NOT_FREE`, `SAME_BODY`, `FACING_MISMATCH`, `WIDTH_MISMATCH`, `CLASS_MISMATCH`, `LANE_MISMATCH`, `GEOM_OVERLAP`); socket state runs FREE, WELDED, CAPPED or CUT_OPEN and never back. The weld offset is `offset_b = offset_a + pos_a - pos_b = (0,0) + (720,672) - (24,288) = (696, 384)`, both components multiples of 24, so B's west hull wall x [24,48) lands at [720,744) abutting the home east wall and B's hatch span y [288,384) lands on [672,768), identical to the home socket (Formula D.13).
182	
183	**DA-11 Hull segments and plate positions.** Every HULL_SEGMENT has a Layout plate-position record (LY-21) and a segment `hp`; segments are 2 tiles (`HULL_SEGMENT_FACE_TILES`) with at least `SEGMENT_GAP_MIN_PX` 96 px between; every outer room has at least `HULL_RUNS_MIN` 2 disjoint exterior wall runs (`OUTER_ROOM_HULL_RUNS` is Layout's). Home 7 segments, A 4, B 5:
184	
185	| Section | Segments (`room_key`: id, authored `hp`) |

291	**DA-13 Derelict time behaviour: three Graph mechanisms, never "dormant until powered".** The thread's sentence ("derelict partitions are dormant until powered, then `DERELICT_FAULT_COMPRESSION` 500 permille applies") maps onto three separate Graph mechanisms, none of which is "dormant until powered":
292	
293	- **(a) Load-dormancy** (LS-17): a section whose derelict is not loaded (zoomed out, left behind) has its slots skipped by every phase, its state frozen, no fast-forward on return, and `can_join` returns `SECTION_NOT_LOADED`. This is driven by *load*, not by power.
294	- **(b) Compression** (LS-25; Graph D.9 derived line): every endogenous `hp` loss on a loaded DERELICT section runs at `rate_pm` = 10^6 / `DERELICT_FAULT_COMPRESSION` = 10^6 / 500 = 2000 (the registry range of the constant is 250 to 1000 permille): wear and overload double; gas physics, heat and supply do not.
295	- **(c) Dead-fault wake** (LS-25): a subject at `hp` at or below `HP_FAIL` on an unserved branch emits `intensity_pm` 0 until power or coolant reaches it.
296	
297	Authoring consequence: a derelict's authored `hp` values are the values the player meets on every return, because (a) freezes them; only the player's acts, the weld, or time spent *loaded* change them. 464	- *Lethal cold (derelict A only).* `a_machine` is authored at `T0` -22000 mC with `forced_mode` FREEZE on its liquid pipes (LSG:764: a derelict "already frozen" is a content fact, not an endogenous transition). The shifted cold onset is -20000 mC (`COLD_DMG_ONSET_MC` -15000 less `INSUL_MC` 5000); the room's equilibrium sits at the plate-term stall, `ceil(100000 / (K_HULL x exposed_tiles))` = ceil(100000 / 325) = 308 mC above `T_AMB_MC` -30000 (about -29692 mC; the Graph's 182 mC is its 22-tile example, not this room), far below the onset, which satisfies Suit's export (SE-21: a lethal cold room must have equilibrium below the shifted onset) `[derived; Graph owner to confirm with LSG D.7, OQ-DA-4]`. Suit's export is why the rule exists: with `INSUL_MC` 5000 an unpowered home-ship needs about 40 minutes to reach the shifted onset (SE-21), so a cold-hazard derelict room must be authored with an equilibrium temperature below the shifted cold onset or it is no hazard. It is the only lethal-cold room in MVP (B's hazard is heat and vacuum; B's heat room is `b_reactor`, next bullet). It is entered from `a_spine` (`T0` -12000 mC) through `door_a_spine_machine`, with a dried frost fan creeping out over the door sill, visible in the beam: the tell precedes the hazard (P2). Crossing is safe and lingering is lethal: at `T0` the room reaches CRITICAL cold in about 36 s and FAILED in about 109 s (Suit's D.4 with the Suit knobs; Formula D.10), so a seven-tile crossing takes 5.6 s carrying while the patch channel inside is the lethal act. The room's heater `htr_a` and the bus battery `b_a2` sit on the branch that the spare breaker wakes. **Feeding the wreck has one computed benefit** (D.22): the heater lifts the room from -22000 mC above the shifted onset -20000 mC after 447 steps (45 s) and holds it out of damaging cold for about 12.9 minutes on the full bus (`b_a2` 1,620,000 dJ), after which it returns to damaging cold, so it is a bus battery's lifetime and not a base. **User ruling (D45, 2026-10-27): this computed window is the whole payoff of waking the branch for the first build, deliberately modest; no powered door, lamps-lit-only fact or second live tell is authored. The X-DA-8 reasons log (AC-DA-135) is the trigger for any later authored payoff, which the creative-director then owns (OQ-DA-43 options B to D)** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*. In-room work is budgeted by `t_work_max` (D.10): 25.2 s at `T0`, 13.8 s after 30 minutes unheated, 6.2 s at the equilibrium, module carried both ways. The junction `j_a_main` sits in `a_machine`: the swap is two channels (about 8 s) plus a 5.6 s crossing, 14 of the 25.2 s at `T0`, and the room needs 447 steps (44.7 s) after the breaker closes to pass the onset, so staying through them accrues about 4,200 of exposure against `TL_CRITICAL` 4,000 (gain 11 falling to 8); the order is swap, close the breaker, step back into `a_spine` for about 45 s and return (whether exposure recovers once the room is above the onset is Suit D.4's, cited and not assumed) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*. The order is safe without any recovery *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*: the 14 s inside accrue at most 140 runs x gain 11 = 1,540, `a_spine` (`T0` -12000 mC) is above the onset and accrues nothing, and on return the room is above the onset too, so the peak is at most 1,540 against `TL_CRITICAL` 4,000 even if exposure never falls; AC-DA-153 checks it on a Suit stub. The quiet alternative (cut `scr_a` in `a_life` and leave) never enters the room, and the crossing at the authored speed is safe either way (D.10) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*. `COLD_ROOM_UNDECLARED` (ERROR): a room whose `T0` is below the shifted onset must be declared lethal, and exactly one per MVP body may be. The "exactly one lethal room" invariant is a *build-state* invariant: opening the door between `a_spine` and `a_machine` mixes them by conduction, so the lint also prints the open-door projection.
465	- *Heat (derelict B, `b_reactor`, after V12; `[derived; Graph owner to confirm Q_src_room]`).* `b_reactor` is authored at `T0` 42000 mC (the HOT band, 40000 and up, LSG:96), 3000 mC under `HEAT_DMG_ONSET_MC` 45000 (registry). Suit's heat axis has no insulation shift (`e_heat` = `T` - `HEAT_DMG_ONSET_MC`, SE D.4), so the room is harmless as authored and its HOT shimmer is the standing tell. A SCRAMmed `r_b` has `Q_src` 0 and `T_mach` = `T_room` (LSG D.8), which is why V12 is not `BLOCKED` `STILL_HOT` (DA-35). **After V12** the restarted reactor leaks the uncaptured part of its heat into the room (`Q_src_room`; 516 dJ per step is the Graph's D.8 worked example, `[UNV: Graph]`) against a hull loss of `K_HULL` x 21 x (`T` - `T_AMB_MC`) / 100000 = 378 dJ per step at 42000 mC: the room reaches 45000 mC after about 2,770 steps (4.6 minutes, `tau_steps` 22,857) and settles near 68,300 mC (D.18). From the fifth minute lingering is damaging: at that equilibrium `e` is 23,286, `gain` is 40, `runs_critical` is 100 (10.0 s) and `runs_failed` 300 (30.0 s) by D.10 with Suit's heat gain; the 8-tile crossing is 192 ticks (3.2 s) walking and 384 ticks (6.4 s) carrying. 757	## Formulas
758	
759	**Conventions.** Authoring has no runtime math of its own (DA-1): every formula below is either a **lint formula** (a pure function of the authored files plus `content_lint_config`, DA-41), a **derivation** that fixes an authored number from a Graph, Item DB or Layout formula (so the number is solved, not guessed), or the **closed form a headless test asserts** (DA-42). All inputs are authored integers. A Graph step is `GRAPH_STEP_TICKS` 6 ticks = 0.1 s, so 600 steps = 1 minute; watts are dJ per step (LSG LS-1). Formula ids `D.1` to `D.22` are fixed by the index in Core Rules and are never renumbered; the Graph's formulas are always written `LSG D.n` (the Graph's own D.15 is the fixture table, this GDD's D.15 is the patch and fatigue treadmill). Nothing here is hashed or replicated; the only transcendental function (D.18's natural logarithm) is lint-side and forbidden on the sim path (LSG LS-1 g), and the lint evaluates it with a fixed-point table so two runs over the same bytes print identical bytes (DA-41). Values resting on a provisional upstream carry `[PLACEHOLDER: owner]` at every mention.
760	
761	### D.1 Tile volume budget per reachable set
762	
763	The `tile_volume_budget` formula is defined as:
764	
765	`world_tiles(S) = sum over every room r of every section in S of V(r) + POD_TILES x pods_loaded(S)` ; `ERROR iff world_tiles(S) > TILES_WORLD_MVP` ; `WARN iff 100 x world_tiles(S) >= WORLD_TILES_WARN_PCT x TILES_WORLD_MVP`
766	
767	**Variables:**
768	| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
769	|---|---|---|---|---|
770	| `V(r)` | int tiles | 4 to 200 | LY D.3 (`room_volume`) | Volume of one compartment; the room tables of C.1 to C.3 are the authored values |
771	| `S` | set of sections | the five reachable sets of DA-32 | DA-32 `[provisional: Web Map & Transit undesigned]` | The sections loaded at the same time |
772	| `POD_TILES` | int tiles | 4 | DA-3 (`pod_cabin` `V` 4) | Added when the persistent pod body exists (always dormant, WM-5); a pod is not in the three-ship totals |
773	| `pods_loaded(S)` | int | 0 or 1 | Web Map & Transit (registry `pod_body`) | Pod bodies in the world (0 before `init_world`, 1 after; the 453 figure includes it) |
774	| `TILES_WORLD_MVP` | int tiles | 600 | LY D.13 (a Layout knob citing FT:598; not a registry entry) | World tile budget |
775	| `WORLD_TILES_WARN_PCT` | int % | 90 | LY D.13 | Warning fraction (WARN at 540 tiles) |
776	
777	**Output Range:** 0 to `TILES_WORLD_MVP` + 4; the MVP content spans 182 (`{home}`) to 453 (all three ships plus a docked pod). Per-section bounds are Layout's (`SECTION_MAX_TILES_W` 48 by `SECTION_MAX_TILES_H` 32, `MAX_ROOMS_PER_SECTION` 8); the authored `size_tiles` are 16 x 18, 17 x 14 and 20 x 18.
778	**Example:** `home_ship` 42 + 39 + 36 + 35 + 30 = 182; `derelict_a` 20 + 33 + 30 + 35 = 118; `derelict_b` 20 + 39 + 40 + 20 + 30 = 149. S0 `{home}` 182 (30.3 %); S1 `{home, A}` 300 (50.0 %); S2 and S3 `{home, B}` 331 (55.2 %); S4 `{home+B, A}` 449 (74.8 %); S4 with a docked pod 453 (75.5 %). Every set sits 87 tiles or more under the 540 WARN line, so `TILE_BUDGET` is silent at MVP and tracks the budget for the Vertical Slice.
779	
780	### D.2 Count tolerance (one-sided)
781	
782	The `count_tolerance` formula is defined as:
783	
784	`over = authored - target` ; `tol = max(floor(target x NODE_DRIFT_PCT / 100), NODE_DRIFT_ABS_MIN)` ; `NODE_COUNT_DRIFT = WARN iff over > tol` ; `INFO iff over < 0` ; `ERROR iff sum of authored nodes over the world > NODE_HARD_MAX`
785	
786	**Variables:**
787	| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
788	|---|---|---|---|---|
789	| `authored` | int | 0 to 120 | the templates (DA-19 ledger) | Count of nodes, design edges or LOAD nodes for one section |
790	| `target` | int | the "about" counts of LSG LS-26 | LSG LS-26 (LSG:228) | Nodes about 40 / 30 / 35 (home / A / B); edges about 55 (home) and about 45 (the B cost row of LSG D.16); LOADs about 8 (home). LS-26 gives A no edge or LOAD target |
791	| `NODE_DRIFT_PCT` | int % | 10 to 30 (20) | Authoring knob | Relative tolerance |
792	| `NODE_DRIFT_ABS_MIN` | int | 2 to 5 (3) | Authoring knob | Absolute floor so a small target is not a hair-trigger |
793	| `NODE_HARD_MAX` | int | 120 | LSG:787 (the Graph's MVP content bound; `MAX_GRAPH_NODES` 4096 and the 800-node WARN of LSG:915 are irrelevant at this scale) | Hard cap on authored nodes in the world |
794	
795	**Output Range:** an INFO, a WARN or a pass per count; below target is never a defect, because the Graph's cost model (LSG D.16) is monotone in count.
796	**Example:** home nodes 42 against 40: over 2, `tol` max(8, 3) = 8, pass. A nodes 27 against 30: over -3, INFO. B nodes 35 against 35: over 0. World nodes 104 against 120: pass. ### D.22 Heater on the bus battery (A's warm window) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: new formula)*

The `bus_heater_window` formula is defined as (a lint and report formula, harness-side; the natural logarithm is forbidden on the sim path and the lint uses the fixed-point table of D.18):

`dT_step = 1000 x (P_htr - q_hull(T)) / (V x C_TILE)` mC per step in fixed-point accumulation (each step's quotient carries its remainder into the next and only the accumulated `T` is floored for comparison; a per-step floor would give 4 mC instead of 4.51 at the start and shorten the full-bus window to about 10.9 minutes, which the table below does not use) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* with `q_hull(T) = K_HULL x S_ext x (T - T_AMB_MC) / 100000` ; `t_onset_steps` = the first step at which `T` exceeds `ONSET_MC` while the heater runs ; `T_end` = `T` after `t_bus_steps` (D.16) ; `t_return_steps = ceil(tau_steps x ln((T_end - T_AMB_MC) / (ONSET_MC - T_AMB_MC)))` (the room cools back with the heater dead) ; `window_steps = max(0, t_bus_steps - t_onset_steps) + t_return_steps` ; `THAW_REACHABLE iff T_end > FREEZE_OFF_MC`

**Variables:**
| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `P_htr` | int W = dJ per step | 500 | `htr_a`, `mod_heater` (all of it is heat, `waste_permille` 1000; other loads' waste is ignored, the conservative side) | Heat into `a_machine` |
| `V`, `S_ext`, `C_TILE`, `K_HULL` | int | 35, 13, 3000, 25 | C.2, D.18 | Room volume, exposed tiles, thermal mass, hull conductance |
| `T0`, `ONSET_MC`, `FREEZE_OFF_MC` | int mC | -22000, -20000, -10000 | C.2; SE D.4; LSG | Start, shifted cold onset, thaw line |
| `tau_steps` | int steps | 32,307 | D.18 | Cooling time constant of `a_machine` |
| `t_bus_steps` | int steps | per D.16 | D.16 | How long the battery feeds the heater |

**Output Range:** `t_onset_steps` is 447 (the heater lifts the room the 2,000 mC to the onset in 44.7 s); `window_steps` runs from 7,768 (12.9 minutes) on the full bus to 28,144 (46.9 minutes) with the heater alone.
**Example** (`b_a2` 1,620,000 dJ, 1000 mC = 1 degC):

| Bus configuration | `t_bus_steps` | `T_end` (mC) | Gain | `t_return_steps` | Window out of damaging cold |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| full bus, `j_a_res` open | 1,012 | -17,502 | 4.5 C | 7,203 (12.0 min) | 7,768 steps = **12.9 min** |
| `scr_a` cut | 1,620 | -14,867 | 7.1 C | 13,385 | 14,558 = 24.3 min |
| pump and heater only | 1,800 | -14,096 | 7.9 C | 14,990 | 16,343 = 27.2 min |
| heater alone (scrubber, pump and lamps shed) | 3,240 | -8,083 | 13.9 C | 25,351 | 28,144 = 46.9 min; `THAW_REACHABLE` |
| full bus, `j_a_res` CLOSED (`b_a1` joins) | 1,333 | -16,105 | 5.9 C | 10,628 | 11,514 = 19.2 min |

Reading: waking the branch buys about 12.9 minutes of unhurried work in the one lethal room, and the pump lantern going dark at step 1,012 is the cue that it ends (the room is back at the onset 12.0 minutes after the stall). It buys nothing else: the scrubber is cut either way, the splice needs no power, and the benefit is bounded by the bus battery and not by the ship. Stated plainly *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*: every in-room act already fits the cold-room work budget without heat (DA-28, D.10), and the reference sortie cuts `htr_a`, which ends the window, so the window enables no act that is otherwise impossible; it buys margin (a fumbled swap, a second look, a slower cut) and nothing more, which is the deliberately modest payoff of user ruling D45, measured by AC-DA-135 with curiosity-only wakes excluded. The window opens only once the room passes the onset, 447 steps (44.7 s) after the breaker closes, and `j_a_main` is inside the room, so the swap is made, the breaker closed and the room left for about 45 s (DA-28). The earlier "about +4 degC in the 90 s window" understated it by leaving out that the room starts only 2 degC under the onset. **Thaw:** `pa_frozen` thaws (above `FREEZE_OFF_MC`) only on the heater-alone row, which needs the scrubber and the pump cut and every lamp switched off (three kinds of act), so it is not an authored route; it is accepted and tagged: with the pump shed there is no flow, so under gated wear the thawed pipe holds `hp` 2500, and the thaw-burst roll of LS-11 is the Graph's `[UNV: Graph]`. With the pump served the thaw needs 2,496,600 dJ, which is 6,600 dJ above the largest pool the knobs allow (`b_a2` at its 1,950,000 ceiling plus `b_a1` 540,000 with `j_a_res` closed = 2,490,000), so a pump-served thaw (and the 13.2-minute wear clock behind it) is out of reach by construction; lint `THAW_REACHABLE` (ERROR, CI) evaluates it on the pooled `C_bus`, `j_a_res` closed, and fails the build if a knob edit makes it reachable *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*. 'Too high' for `A_BUS_BATTERY_DJ` is therefore not 'A becomes a base' (a full 3,600,000 dJ cell lasts 2,250 steps = 3.75 minutes on the full bus) but that ceiling. The decision whether this computed window is a sufficient reason to wake the branch, or whether an authored payoff is wanted as well, is OQ-DA-43.

1672	
1673	This system has no input and no frame of its own, so its feel is the feel of what the authored data makes happen: how soon a player's act is answered by a lamp, a pipe or a trail, how long a tell lasts before a clock ends, how far a player can run to a door, and how heavy a carry across a dead room is. Every number below is either authored here, derived from an authored value by a formula in this GDD, or cited from the owner (never restated as ours). The playtest targets at the end are `[PLACEHOLDER: creative-director]` until the first playtest.
1674	
1675	### Input-to-feedback chain (the content-shaped acts)
1676	
1677	| Step | What happens | Latency | Owner |
1678	|---|---|---|---|
1679	| 1 | The player holds `interact` on a breaker (V3), valve (V5), fitting (V1) or crank (V12). The acknowledgement is immediate; the channel bar fills linearly | 0 ticks to the bar; V1 `PATCH_CHANNEL_TICKS` 180 (3 s) `[PLACEHOLDER: Interaction]`; V12 `CRANK_CHANNEL_TICKS` 240 (4 s); V3 and V5 per Interaction | Interaction, Player Controller |
1680	| 2 | The completed act calls its Graph mutator (M7, M11, M13 and the like) in the kernel's command path | applied inside the same tick it completes (kernel P-phase), never drawn before commit | Interaction, kernel |
1681	| 3 | The Graph hook chain (`graph.propagate.power`, `.atmo`, `.failure`) runs at divisor 6, so the new `served_pm` is visible to the Emitter and the presentation at the next Graph step | at most `GRAPH_STEP_TICKS` 6 ticks = 100 ms after step 2 | Graph |
1682	| 4 | The Emitter marks the fixture lit; Lighting warms it over `LAMP_WARM_FRAMES` (placeholder 5 frames, `[PLACEHOLDER: Lighting]`) with the prompt edge and the visible edge agreeing from the first frame (LO-19) | 5 presentation frames, about 83 ms at 60 Hz | Lighting |
1683	| 5 | The pipe pattern on the newly served branch starts to move; frost, drip and trail respond at their own cadences (F&T) | one Graph step per hop, so a wake travels down a pipe at 10 hops per second | Pipeline, F&T |
1684	
1685	So the answer to "I closed the breaker" is a lit room within about 12 frames of the channel completing, and the whole branch following hop by hop inside a second or two: fast enough to read as the player's cause, slow enough to watch the effect travel (P1: the pipe agrees with the gauge). What Authoring contributes to this chain is the content that makes it legible: `fx_cryo_2` is `switch_on` true behind the breaker `j_cryo` (open at wake), so the room floods with no new command (EM-13); the branch is short (the cryo branch cable `cab_cryo` is the first thing the breaker feeds); and the frost trail, the dark heater and the dim lamp are all in one frame of the wake room.
1686	
1687	### Content timings the feel rests on (all derived, with the source)
1688	
1689	| Quantity | Value | Derivation |
1690	|---|---|---|
1691	| Cryo wake: lamp gutter | 18 to 30 tick dips, no more often than every 600 to 1200 ticks | ART 2.2 as authored in E2 (Lighting's `gutter_recipe` owns the generator) |
1692	| Warm-up of the cryo bay after V3 | the room warms at about 4 mC per Graph step gross (500 W into C = 42 x `C_TILE` 3000 = 126,000 dJ/°C, LSG D.7), about 3 mC net of hull loss at 13 exposed tiles, so about 6.5 minutes (about 3,900 Graph steps, about 23,400 ticks) from -2000 mC to COMFORT at 10000 mC; LSG:839's 2.5 minutes is its 20-tile example. The slower climb is the price of the verbatim Layout fixture (V 42, 13 exposed tiles); a second heater is the PWR-OVL trigger (DA-15 #3), so `CRYO_HEATER_COUNT` stays 1 | DA-45, D.18 warm-up line, LSG D.7 |
1693	| Every endogenous failure's tell | 600 to 1,800 ticks (10 to 30 s), never under `W_MIN_WARNING_S` 10 s = 600 ticks | P2; the Graph's fairness gate on endogenous transitions (DA-29) |
1694	| Longest escape route to a closable door | 1,800 px = `W_MIN_WARNING_S` x `TICK_RATE` x `V_RUN` (10 x 60 x 3): 10 s at a run, 15 s at `V_WALK` 2 | `ESCAPE_ROUTE_BUDGET_PX` (Layout D.19); authored longest is `pf_feed`, about 480 px, 160 ticks at a run (D.5) |
1695	| One-way crossing of `a_machine` carrying a module | 7 tiles = 336 px at `V_CARRY` 1 px/tick = 336 ticks = 5.6 s | D.10: critical after 364 runs (36.4 s) at `T0`, so a crossing leaves a margin of about 31 s |
1696	| Longest vacuum or cold round trip carrying a module | 56 tiles = 2,688 px = 2,688 ticks = 44.8 s round trip, 28 tiles each way (the lint bound; B's worst case 40 tiles = 32 s round trip) | D.7 (`TRAVERSE_TOO_LONG`) |
1697	| Reference carry (`htr_a` cut point to the pod in `a_dock`) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)* | ruled 21 to 28 tiles = 1,008 to 1,344 px = 16.8 to 22.4 s at `V_CARRY` 1; provisional 28 tiles (1,344 px, 22.4 s: n = 12, d = 24) `[PLACEHOLDER — derive at spike]` *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*; today's plan is 13 tiles (624 ticks, 10.4 s) | DA-48 |
1698	| Fuel Ember clock from wake | FAILED no earlier than 10 minutes (6,000 Graph steps' worth: 36,000 ticks), SCRAM recoverable | DA-16, amended R5 |
1699	| Pump-stall tell on A (full bus, `b_a2`) | 1,012 Graph steps = 6,072 ticks = 101 s of served pump before the stall (the 900-step target met with 112 steps to spare) | D.16 |
1700	| A's lethal room out of damaging cold after waking the branch | about 12.9 minutes on the full bus (447 steps to the onset, then 12.0 minutes of return after the stall) | D.22 |
1701	| Seam breaker closed onto a dead B | lamps dim at once, `cab_trunk` DEGRADED at step 334 (33 s), FAILED at 778 (78 s), DESTROYED at 1,112 (111 s); re-open before 778 and the trunk survives | DA-20, D.9 |
1702	| Heat tell on B (`b_reactor`, after V12) | presentation step at `HEAT_TELL_STEP_MC` 44,700 mC 2,477 Graph steps (4.1 minutes) after V12, 293 steps (29.3 s, 1,758 ticks) before damage starts at 2,770; never under 100 steps (600 ticks) | D.18 tell lead, DA-28, AC-DA-133 `(provisional)` |
1703	| Hull-fatigue tell on B | `seg_b_pump_n` crosses `BREACH_HP` after 30 periods (3,000 steps = 5 minutes of B-loaded time); hairline to crack to bent rib is visible for at least 10 s before the breach (P2) | D.20, D.15 |
1704	| Patch hold before decay | `PATCH_DECAY_STEPS` 2400 = 4 minutes; a patched home leak is back at `LEAK_HP` in 4,500 steps (7.5 minutes), a derelict one in 3,500; the felt cost of this treadmill is target X-DA-9 (below), whose levers are `PATCH_DECAY_STEPS` (Graph-owned) and the home leak count | D.15, DA-25 |
1705	| Restart race on B | the patch on `pb_leak` lands within `W` 90 s of V12; the stock crosses the floor at 123.8 s (step 1,238) and the tank is empty at 211 s; V12 channel 4 s *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* | D.21 |
1706	| Residual lamps | A 27,000 steps = 162,000 ticks = 45 minutes loaded; B 21,600 steps = 36 minutes loaded | D.6 |
1707	| Beacon revolution | `BEACON_SWEEP_TICKS` 128 `[PLACEHOLDER: Emitter]` = 2.13 s | Emitter registry |
1708	| Door leaf | slides whole pixels per tick; it travels in the same tick the Graph's `area` changes (0 ticks of Layout latency) | LY-9, Layout latency row |
1709	| Weld seam: fresh to old | `SEAM_OLD_AFTER_TICKS` 36,000 (10 minutes) | ART 6.1 |
1710	
1711	### Weight and snap

- **Whole-pixel everything.** Leaves, plates, dust and trails move or sit on whole pixels at the integer zoom rungs; a placed prop sits on the 24 px lattice (LY-3), so a player never sees a prop one pixel off a wall. Snap target: zero sub-pixel positions in any authored record (`AUTHORED_NON_INTEGER`, `WELD_OFFSET` lattice check D.13).
- **The carry is the weight.** A module is carried at `V_CARRY` 1 (a third of a run, half a walk). The authored salvage is placed so the round trip through an unbreathable stretch to the farthest salvage and back is at most 56 tiles (44.8 s at `V_CARRY`) and the farthest hazard crossing at most 7 tiles of lethal cold (5.6 s): heavy enough to feel like a burden and a decision about the route, short enough to be fair. No authored carry route passes within 1 tile of a fault's maximum floor run.
- **Nothing decorative moves.** The only moving things in a dead wreck are the player's beam and its dust; the only sound-shaped event is a lamp, a drip or a hum that the Graph is actually producing. That stillness is the weight of a wreck.
- **No hit-stop, shake or flash is authored.** Failure is felt through the tell (a longer-lasting visible trail and a changing pipe), not through an effect on the camera.

### The three authored beats (anchor moments as feel)

1. **The cryo wake (first minute).** Slowest, quietest frame in the game: ambient about 3 %, one gutter dip every 10 to 20 s, a drip as the fastest motion, a frost line the eye follows to a fitting. The player closes `j_cryo`, the room floods warm in about 12 frames, the heater begins its 6.5-minute climb (about 4 mC per Graph step gross, D.18; the price of the verbatim Layout fixture), and the player patches the fitting in 3 s of channel. Beside the door the shut valve `v_o2_cryo` waits in the same sweep: a player who lingers meets the thinning air at 7.0 minutes with the valve in view, and the first valve they turn is a lever with a price (V5, DA-45) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*. The door opens onto a lit corridor with the beacon dark; `door_engine_n` stands open and the ember glow of `pf_feed` is the next thing in view. No text, no marker (DA-45). "Warmth is spent, not owned": the flood of Tungsten is an event the player caused and paid for in power.
2. **The held-breath boarding (derelict A, first sortie).** From the pod, A is black but for one Tungsten point (the residual lamp). Arrival room: beam only, dust in the cone, a dried coolant fan at a lagged elbow. The eye follows trail, source, hatch (ART 6.5 eye line). One sweep tells the player who built it, what was done to it, and that the web has not come in. The decision beat is the dead branch: swapping the spare `mod_breaker_junction` wakes the bus, lights the pump's lantern (the FAILED scrubber's stays dark, DA-24), starts the pump-stall clock (about 100 s of tell, D.16) and doubles the speed of every wear row (`DERELICT_FAULT_COMPRESSION` 500). The cost lands as the player's own consequence, not an ambush.
3. **The weld seam (derelict B, then home).** B is hot and loud in the dark: a SCRAM rim glow, a draught from a vacuum room, a fatigued segment with a visible hairline-to-crack tell, a restart race with a 90 s window. After the weld the player stands at the doubled bulkhead and can say which side was the original ship without a prompt (Layout X-1, AC-DA-07).

### Playtest-checkable targets

The creative-director ruling (CD-GDD-ALIGN) endorses X-DA-1 to X-DA-7 as written and adds X-DA-8 and X-DA-9; the design review adds X-DA-10. The targets themselves are fixed; only the numeric thresholds are `[PLACEHOLDER: creative-director]` (tagged inline). Each round is **five testers, at least three of whom are outside the project**, matching the concept's kill/continue gate ("at least three people outside the project", game-concept MVP Definition). Five testers and 4-of-5 thresholds are a smoke signal, not a statistic: a second round of 8 or more is required before any threshold below is promoted from placeholder `[PLACEHOLDER: creative-director]`. Protocols and scoring sheets are in Acceptance Criteria (AC-DA-87 to AC-DA-93, AC-DA-135 to AC-DA-137), AC-DA-151). **The re-review adds X-DA-11** (the first scrubber install, DA-47). **Which beats a 30-minute session can test** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*: the concept's kill/continue session is about 30 minutes, which holds the home wake (X-DA-4, X-DA-7), the first sortie to A with its read, decision and carry home (X-DA-1, X-DA-2, X-DA-3, X-DA-6, X-DA-8) and the first install (X-DA-11 when `scr_a` is carried); the weld and the first B sortie (X-DA-5, X-DA-10) fall at about 45 to 55 minutes and the treadmill (X-DA-9) needs 45, so they are run in a separate session that starts from a save past the first sortie, and the 3

| Id | Target |
|---|---|
| X-DA-1 | At least 4 of 5 `[PLACEHOLDER: creative-director]` first-time testers name the failed loop of derelict A within 60 s of boarding, from the dried trails alone, and point at the trail that told them *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* |
| X-DA-2 | At least 4 of 5 `[PLACEHOLDER: creative-director]` point at the residual light during transit and find its room aboard within 3 minutes without a marker |
| X-DA-3 | At least 3 of 5 `[PLACEHOLDER: creative-director]` pause (coded with gaze or utterance, AC-DA-89) or voice a cost before closing A's breaker or swapping its junction *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* |
| X-DA-4 | No tester is stationary and lost for more than 30 s in the cryo bay; at least 4 of 5 `[PLACEHOLDER: creative-director]` follow the frost trail to its fitting unprompted |
| X-DA-5 | Layout X-1 as written (seam-side identification), cited not restated; AC-DA-07 and AC-DA-91 |
| X-DA-6 | At least 3 of 5 `[PLACEHOLDER: creative-director]` testers, given the neutral prompt "tell me about what you took and what you left", answer about choice or risk, not an inventory display *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* |
| X-DA-7 | The door state (open or closed) is identified correctly from three tiles in greyscale by at least 4 of 5 `[PLACEHOLDER: creative-director]` reviewers |
| X-DA-8 | Restraint is a real strategy (P3): across 5 testers both the wake-the-branch and the leave-it-dark outcome on A occur at least once, and every tester who left it dark returned home having taken the cut by beam, and can say why they carried it or left it; the observer also logs, for every tester, the reason given for waking the branch or leaving it dark (the AC-DA-135 coding), so that a branch nobody wakes for the D.22 window shows as a false choice *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* |
| X-DA-9 | The patch treadmill is not a chore (P5 against the MVP core hypothesis): fewer than 2 of 5 `[PLACEHOLDER: creative-director]` testers describe re-patching the home leaks as tedious or a chore in the first 45 minutes, and the observer-timed share of active maintenance (channels plus walking to the leaks) in minutes 10 to 45 is at most 8 % with the plate carried and 16 % without it (D.15 computes 4.9 to 6.8 % and 12.8 to 14.7 %) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*. Levers if it fails: `PATCH_DECAY_STEPS` (Graph-owned, a routed ask) and the home leak count (3); the ledger is not changed before the playtest (DA-25) |
| X-DA-10 | A first-time tester's first sortie to derelict B (a restart race of about 2.1 minutes after V12, the floor crossing at step 1,238 (D.21) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review: was "a 3.5-minute restart race", a constant-leak figure; this pass bar, not a derived constant, sets the race length, OQ-DA-50)*, a hull breach at 5.0 minutes and decompression at 6.7 minutes of B-loaded time, reachable before any plate is carried): at least 4 of 5 `[PLACEHOLDER: creative-director]` testers restart `r_b` (V12) and finish the sortie without a SCRAM-recovery prompt, at most 1 of 5 close the seam breaker onto a dead B, and the SCRAM-recovery sub-case of AC-DA-59 is observed *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* |
| X-DA-11 | The first scrubber install at home is a taught order, not a silent run-ender (DA-47): of 5 first-time testers who carry `scr_a` home and install it with the cryo branch closed, at most 1 `[PLACEHOLDER: creative-director]` loses `cab_trunk` (DESTROYED), and at least 4 of 5 who see the tell shed the cryo branch or remove the scrubber before FAILED (step 875; 778 with the beacon lit); if more than 1 of 5 lose it, the install interlock of DA-47 option (c) is built (OQ-DA-47) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* |

## Cross-References

Citation forms: LSG = `life-support-graph.md`; LY = `ship-section-and-layout-data-model.md`; IDB = `item-and-module-database.md`; EM = `emitter-state-and-light-exposure-query.md`; FT = `failure-and-trail-system.md`; LO = `2d-lighting-and-occlusion.md`; IA = `interaction-system.md`; SE = `suit-and-equipment.md`; SL = `save-load-and-versioned-format.md`; PIPE = `pixel-perfect-render-pipeline-camera.md`; PCI = `player-controller-input.md`; BDY = `ship-body-and-interior-physics.md`; KRN = `command-simulation-layer.md`;

#### 1. Declared dependencies on other GDDs' specific rules and values

#### 2. CONFLICT paragraphs and routed wording fixes (nothing below edits another GDD)

- **CONFLICT C-1, the weld donor (LSG vs LY).** LY-13 ("exactly one socket on the home-ship ... and its mate on derelict B"), Layout's `fixture_derelict_b_socket` and IA D.10 ("home ship plus derelict B loaded", the weld case) all name derelict **B** as the donor; one Graph acceptance clause (LSG:1133) says "the section salvaged from derelict A" while its own parenthesis ("D.16's 35/45/5 cost row is the derelict-B worst case") already assumes B. Adopted: **A yields a module, B yields the welded section** (DA-2). Th
- **CONFLICT C-2, "spawn".** LSG:228 tags derelict A "(cold wreck, spawn)" and LY:162 reads "the spawn room for derelict A", while the cryo bay and the wake are in the home-ship (LSG:228, LSG:839). Adopted: the home-ship is the spawn derelict; `entry_room_key` has **one** meaning, the room the pod arrives in (DA-6). Route one-line corrections: LSG:228 "cold wreck, spawn" to "cold wreck, first sortie"; LY:162 "the spawn room for derelict A" to "the pod-arrival room for derelict A".
- **CONFLICT C-3 (closed 2026-10-27):** the registry unit string was corrected in the consistency pass and no longer carries 'once powered'; no wording note is owed.
- **CONFLICT C-4, hardpoints (resolved 2026-10-27).** `home_ship` needs 29 hardpoints (26 module nodes including the beacon lamp `bcn_main` + the vacant `hp_cargo_heater` + the two vacant scrubber slots of DA-47, user ruling D72 *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*; world 69); the registry default `MAX_HARDPOINTS_PER_SECTION` was raised from 24 to 32 (range 12 to 64), so no waiver or removal is needed. Route 2 (remove three home vents) is not taken.
- **CONFLICT C-5, wear vocabulary (ruling R23 vs FT-3 / FT AC-44).** R23 listed "scorch/soot" in `_worn`; adopted narrowed vocabulary (DA-5). Route to the art-director: the bible's 6.2 weathering vocabulary lists scorch as a *Graph-driven trail*; no kit tile carries it.

content.content:
## UI Requirements

**Derelict Authoring has no UI of its own; every surface that shows an authored object is owned by another GDD.** It authors files, not a screen: no HUD element, instrument, menu, prompt, marker, map overlay or notification is named or implied here, and none may be inferred from a field in a template. This is a design decision (P1, P3, the anti-pillars and DA-37), not an omission: the world is the display, so a wreck's richness, danger and history are shown by a lit room, a dried trail, a pipe that agrees with its gauge and one warm point in the dark, never by a rating, a "salvage value", an objective marker, a minimap pin, a "cleared" tick, an icon on the visible unknown or a danger meter f

What touches a player-facing surface, and who owns it:

| Authored fact | Shown by | Owner |
|---|---|---|
| Lamps, residual light, beacon, glowsticks, lanterns | the world, as light | Emitter State, Lighting |
| Faults, dried trails, frost, hole, airflow | the world, as trails and glow rows | Failure & Trail |
| Module `hp` and condition, loose items | the sprite and the interact prompt | Item DB, Interaction |
| Door and hatch state | the leaf sprite | Layout (PROJECTOR) |
| Gauges and instruments reading authored systems | the in-world instruments and the inspect card, corruptible and falsifiable | In-World Instruments & Inspect View (K-4); placement is Authoring's (DA-34, IW-31) |
| The exterior view of a wreck and its `visible_unknown` | the transit view | Web Map & Transit (undesigned) |
| Save, death restart | the pause panel and the failure stub | Save/Load |
| The content lint report | **plain text in the developer console and CI log**; not a player surface and not part of a release build's UI | Authoring (DA-40, DA-41) |

There is therefore no UX Flag for this system and no `/ux-design` pass is required for it. Two constraints are handed to the owners above, both as content rules this GDD enforces by lint: in MVP no authored piece, template or lint message may carry text, a label, an icon or an arrow (VA-13, AC-DA-53; VA-13 targets UI-like markers, not future diegetic lore fragments, which are the narrative-director's), and no authored record may carry a field whose only use is to be drawn on a HUD. A UI that wants to display more about a wreck has to find it in the world first (P1).
### Art-side acceptance criteria, mapped

The art-director's twelve checks are carried in Acceptance Criteria under these ids: sanity palette AC-DA-51; monochrome wreck AC-DA-52; X-1 side identification AC-DA-07; the three ART 6.0 questions AC-DA-93 (a); fault falsifier rows AC-DA-50; wake single light AC-DA-33; visible-unknown port and competitor AC-DA-37; dried-stop contrast and step AC-DA-125; wear, hole, pipe-band and source lints AC-DA-06, AC-DA-49; exterior single lit point AC-DA-38; power-restored static-then-moving pipes and the no-mask lamp AC-DA-126; piece-count reconciliation AC-DA-55.

### Audio: what the authored objects emit (citation only)

Adaptive Audio is undesigned, so this GDD authors no audio rule, layer, ducking, fade or trigger. The authored objects emit exactly what their owners' descriptors say: node lanterns hum while their machine runs (EM-14), B's SCRAM rim ticks as it decays (F&T row 9), a leak hisses with its flow, and an authored hull segment may groan before it fails (the tell is visual; whether and how it sounds is the audio-director's). The mood the visuals set for the audio-director to match: a dead wreck is still, dusty and archaeological; a woken branch is a slow rhythmic hum; the cryo bay is hushed and the drip is the loudest thing in it. Perception Filter audio lies are the Filter's and never live in an authored file.

📌 **Asset Spec** — Visual/Audio requirements are defined. After the art bible is approved, run `/asset-spec system:derelict-authoring-handmade-kits` to produce per-asset visual descriptions, dimensions and generation prompts from this section (the K-1 to K-9 pieces and the `_worn` derivation first).
